title: Tenant Gradual Quantization and Cost Safety Prober
author: Marco Nguyen
description:
Summary: Implements a tenant-aware gradual quantization orchestrator plus a cost-safety prober. The feature allows us to safely roll tenants through lower-bit quantization profiles in progressive steps, measure unit-econ impact and quality regressions via a lightweight canary scoring service, and automatically rollback when SLOs or quality thresholds are violated.

Motivation: Many tenants can tolerate lower-precision models for large portions of traffic; existing single-shot quant rollout tooling is risky. This PR provides a conservative, observable, and reversible path that reduces per-token cost while preserving application quality.

Key capabilities added:
1) Orchestrator: stateful controller that keeps per-tenant rollout state, step schedule, and recent metrics windows.
2) Canary scorer: lightweight evaluator that runs sampled requests through baseline and quantized models and computes a delta score (latency, perplexity proxy, embedding drift).
3) Safety prober: decision logic that enforces rollback if cost/quality trade-offs exceed configured thresholds.
4) Tenant heuristics: default progressive profiles based on tenant traffic shape, e.g., "cold-heavy" vs "burst-heavy".
5) Telemetry: new metrics and events for each step so Console can display rollout health and unit economics.

Checklist:
- [x] Orchestrator core logic implemented
- [x] Canary scorer and sampling hooks

- [x] Docs stub in redwood-docs (follow-up PR will add user guide)

Commits (high level):
- "orchestrator: add tenant gradual quant state machine and API handlers"
- "scorer: implement canary scoring and sample adapter"
- "safety: add rollback rules and SLAs enforcement"
- "telemetry: emit rollout and econ metrics"
- "tests: add e2e flow and unit tests for decision logic"

Changed areas (high-level):
- inference/quant/orchestrator.py: new controller implementing per-tenant state machine and scheduling.
- inference/quant/scorer.py: canary scoring library and adapters for streaming vs batch.
- infra/helm/values-quant.yaml: defaults for progressive rollout (default step intervals, thresholds).
- console/telemetry/events.py: new rollout events and unit econ metrics.
- tests/e2e/test_quant_rollout.py: integration tests that simulate tenant traffic and assert rollback/complete flows.
- docs/stubs/gradual-quant.md: brief explainer (to be expanded in follow-up).

Example of the progressive step API call (pseudo): apply_quant_step(tenant_id, step_profile)  # returns new state/metrics_state

The single-string description continues with review notes and outcomes below.

Review conversation highlights:
- Lena Kim: "Can you ensure rollback decision uses a 95th-percentile latency window and not only mean? Also please surface the exact sample size used for the canary scorer in logs." — Author reply: "Addressed: switched to p95 windows and added logging for effective sample size; updated tests to assert p95 behavior."
- Omar Rodriguez: "We should not change production defaults without a long warmup; ensure helm defaults keep rollout disabled for existing tenants." — Author reply: "Default helm values now set progressive_rollout.enabled=false; cluster admins must opt-in per-tenant. Added infra/helm/values-quant.yaml docs comments."
- Priya Shah: "The scoring metric uses an embedding drift heuristic — can we gate it behind a feature flag for customers that do not send embeddings?" — Author reply: "Added check in scorer and a tenant capability flag (tenant_capabilities.has_embeddings) to skip that comparator when absent."

Requested changes and follow-ups (done in this PR or filed separately):
- Add p95 windows (done).
- Ensure default helm opt-out (done).
- Add console guide and screenshots (follow-up ENG-8921).
- Add longer canary duration option for large tenants (added as configurable param; default conservative).

CI: Initial run failed on a flaky e2e test (random seed mismatch). Reran with fixed test harness and all checks passed.

CI checks:
- unit: pass
- lint: pass (minor formatting fixes applied)
- integration-e2e: pass (stabilized with deterministic sampling)
- helm-lint: pass
- perf-smoke: pass

Merge: Squash merged into main via web UI on 2024-10-14.

Backwards compatibility and safety:
- No breaking API changes to public inference APIs.
- Orchestrator runs independently and does not touch default model routing unless tenant opt-in is enabled.
- Config defaults are conservative (rollout disabled by default).

Observability and release notes: instrumentation added for rollout_start, rollout_step_complete, rollback_triggered, canary_score.{latency,drift,quality_delta}, cost_delta. These make it possible to build a Console view showing unit economics trade-offs per tenant. Metrics naming follows existing tedx.quant.* conventions.

Testing notes:
- Added targeted unit tests for the state machine and scorer comparator with synthetic traces.
- e2e harness simulates 3 tenant archetypes and asserts final state and rollback behavior.

Rollout plan:
- Merge to main, enable in staging via helm flag, run 2-week soak with targeted tenants and dashboards.
- After soak, enable opt-in for production customers and monitor for regressions.

Release notes (short): "Introduce tenant-gradual-quant orchestrator and canary scoring to enable safe progressive quantization rollouts and automatic cost/quality rollbacks. Disabled by default; cluster admins must opt-in per-tenant."

Additional context: This PR is intentionally conservative: it focuses on safety of progressive quantization rather than aggressive autotune.

Follow-up work planned:
1) automated profile suggestion engine (ENG-9420) that recommends step sequences per tenant,
2) a Console UX flow to manage in-flight rollouts (ENG-8921).
